description: No brand mark seen on two current products beyond the printed name.
note: Checked on adamlippes.com: Leighton dress (black floral) and Joan top (ruby floral silk). Leighton text mentions a branded D-ring belt buckle, a minor detail, not a recognised tell. Photos show no logo or patch. Web search found nothing naming a tell.

tell: Trapezoid shape on clasps and bags
description: Akris's own page calls the trapezoid its logo-less logo, seen in clasp and buckle shapes, cut lines and the outline of the Ai bag.
placement: clasps and buckles; Ai bag silhouette; cut lines
note: Brand Trapezoid page opened; it says the trapezoid was adopted in 2009 for accessories, but it is unclear if that dates the tell, so since is ND. Ai XL shoulder tote photo shows the trapezoid bag shape; product text has no trapezoid mention. A consent pop-up covered part of the page and was left alone. A Wallpaper article appeared in search results and was not opened. Subtle: not something a casual observer spots.

description: No mark seen on two current ties beyond a small tag.
note: Checked on alanflusser.com: purple stripe tie and rich navy regimental stripe tie, plus the neckwear page. Ordinary striped silk ties. Brand is a custom clothier. Search found only eBay and Wikipedia, no press on a tell.

description: Leather pieces such as belts and shoes are laser-cut into a scalloped, lace-like perforated edge.
placement: belts, shoes and bags (edge and body of the leather)
note: Real site is maison-alaia.com (the worklist-style maisonalaia.com did not resolve). Bustier Belt in Perforated Vienne Calfskin: screenshot shows the scalloped laser-cut edge; text names only perforated Vienne leather. Retailers in search (not on the press list) also feature it. Also: eyelet pieces (not checked).

description: No mark seen on two current products.
note: Checked on altuzarra.com: Mini Cubetto bag (plain black) and Harburg jacket (double-breasted cotton, tonal buttons). Search returned retailers only. The Cubetto cube bag is a signature product, not a tell.

description: A small MA monogram icon at the chest of current pieces, alongside the bandana paisley print.
note: Raised to medium per Sebastian's ruling: the product text of the MA Bandana Printed Down Vest says MA icon at the chest, beyond the lapel pin on the sport blazer. Homepage items also include a Multi Bandana zip hoodie and Bandana Fairisle beanie, so bandana is the other big mark (also: bandana paisley print). MX1 jean not checked. Site search was blocked by a sign-up pop-up, left alone. No press opened.

description: No mark seen on two current pumps beyond the printed name.
note: Checked on aquazzura.com: Essence Pump 105 (black suede) and Uptown Sling Pump 65 (black). Plain pumps, no callout. Wild Thing fringed sandal is a signature product; fringe not checked on a sandal page.

description: NC
note: Wall: a 10 percent-off pop-up on ariat.com covered the page and blocked the Men menu; left alone, no product pages opened. Search returned retailer listings and brand history pages only. Needs a second pass.

description: A set of curved stripes sweeps across the side panel of the shoe.
note: Seen on the Gel-Slowcush product photos; page text does not name the stripes. End Clothing and Sneaker Freaker pieces appeared in search and were not opened. Strictly a stripe device, not the name in lettering. Brand name on tongue and heel not checked.

description: No mark seen on two current jackets; the brand is described as logo-free.
note: Checked on aspesi.com: double wool field jacket and mini field jacket in dry wax canvas. Text mentions only a hot-stamp zip puller, shoulder tabs, onion-pattern lining and press studs. A Dazed piece titled anti-logomania appeared in search and was not opened. A reseller listing mentions a detachable logo on the mini field jacket; not confirmed. Screenshots lagged, so I relied on page text.

description: The brand uses a crown-over-lowercase-a emblem, shown large on the back of a jacket on the homepage.
note: Opened the homepage (FW26 jacket with the emblem) and the Made for the World Tee: large AWAKE block-letter graphic and a small blue neck label. No source confirms any of these as the recognised tell, so unclear. Retailers list Crown Polo and Crown Logo T-Shirt; not opened. Also: blue neck label.

description: Product copy calls its Nuke thermo-welding a signature: panels bonded by heat instead of stitching.
note: Opened the Matador 3-in-1 jacket (no signature named) and Pyramid jacket (copy says signature Nuke thermo-welding). A sign-up pop-up covered the pages, so the welding was not seen. No press source. The technique is shared with other ski brands and may not identify the brand.

description: The brand name in its own handwritten script, embroidered small on the left chest.
note: Counts only under the distinctive-lettering ruling. Performance Mock Neck photo shows the white script on the chest; the waffle hoodie text mentions an outline mark on a snapback. No press confirms the script is recognised on sight (search returned golf retailers). Bold prints are the signature product. A shop pop-up was left alone.

description: No single garment mark confirmed; the all-caps wordmark may be the recognised logo but looks like an ordinary heavy sans.
note: Opened the homepage and men's new arrivals; the bomber, trousers and sweater looked unmarked. Search returned authentication guides and resellers only. Bags (Le City) are the signature product. Needs a deeper pass for a firm ruling.

tell: The red and white Bally Stripe
description: Bally's About Us page lists the red-and-white Bally Stripe as a house signifier, on straps and trims.
note: About Us names the stripe and, separately, the symmetrical 1851 hardware (also: 1851 hardware). The Ray crossbody page shows a red-toned strap but its text does not mention a stripe and it is out of stock, so no product example given.

description: Blazers close with six gold buttons, double-breasted, stamped with a lion and chain motif.
placement: front closure and cuffs of blazers
note: Product text lists Double Chain Lion gold buttons, six on the front (five decorative) and five on the cuffs. An editorial titled the house signature six-button blazer was seen in search, but it redirected to the homepage so I did not read it. The site served the AE storefront (en-ae URLs).

description: A calligraphic script engraved into the leather, which the product copy calls an iconic Berluti motif.
placement: across leather uppers and leather goods
note: Galet Oxford page (UAE site) refers to the iconic Scritto motif; a location pop-up covered the image, so the script was not seen. The engraved-calligraphy wording comes from the product name plus general knowledge, hence medium. Mr Porter, Hublot and Harry Rosen listings in search were not opened. Also: Venezia leather patina.

description: Garments are built from or appliquéd with vintage domestic textiles, so pieces read as patchwork.
placement: across the body of shirts and outerwear
note: Equestrian Patch Long Sleeve Shirt text says appliquéd with domestic textiles. A design approach and product signature, not a single mark seen at a glance, so unclear. No press opened.

description: A B-shaped zipper puller used on its jackets since 1955, later also a trademark on other goods.
placement: zipper pullers on ski jackets and outerwear
note: Brand page The Zipper that Made History names it and gives the year, credited to Maria Bogner. I did not see the B puller on the Bahri jacket: a cookie banner covered the photos and the text does not mention it. Also: BOGNER name printed vertically on sleeves (photo only).

description: Leather strips woven into a basket-like surface, which the brand's pages call the house signature.
placement: all over bags, wallets and some shoes
note: Corso collection page calls it the signature Intrecciato weave; the Corso tote page mentions Intrecciato leather and the weave is visible in screenshots. A Vogue Singapore article appeared in search and was not opened. No start year verified (1966 is commonly cited, unsourced here).

description: The emblem is a line drawing of a head with the name inside, used as the site logo and named Logohead on hats.
note: Opened the homepage, the apparel collection, the Collegiate Mercerized Track Jacket (Brain Dead typography in tackle twill on the back) and the Ribbed Envelope Baby Tee (embroidered typography on the chest). The head emblem was seen in the site header and in Logohead 6 Panel Hat names, not on a garment. Custom lettering could qualify. No press source.

description: No mark seen on two current suits.
note: Checked on brioni.com: Brunico glen plaid suit and Iride herringbone Plume suit. The script logo shows on the site header, not as a garment mark I could find. Interior labels not checked. Search returned authentication guides and forums only.

description: No mark seen on two current knit pieces; the brand is described as logo-free.
note: Checked on shop.brunellocucinelli.com: cashmere crewneck sweater and cashmere mariner cardigan; both plain in photos with no logo in the text. An Alizila article titled as no logos and a Mr Porter Journal piece appeared in search and were not opened. The women's beaded trim (monili) was not checked.

description: A business stripe pairing a black hairline and a white self stripe with a dominant colour stripe; the brand calls it perhaps its calling card.
note: Collection text says the original stripe dates back 100 years and hangs in the Piccadilly shop; calling card is hedged and from the brand only. Product page calls it an iconic Budd stripe. No press confirmation; Rake and Permanent Style results were not opened. Pop-ups left alone. Also: the Budd collar (not examined).

description: A hood fitted with two goggle lenses at the front, a design the brand introduced in 1988.
note: Brand Goggle Jacket page says introduced in 1988 and calls it a symbol of the brand. The Chrome-R goggle down jacket page shows the lens hood. A Hypebeast piece appeared in search and was not opened. Also: the lens-and-C.P. badge (not opened).
